name: Nóine
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Noine, also spelled Noindiu or Noidhiu, is an Irish folkloric figure. He was a child carried for nine years before birth. In one tale a water spirit seduced his mother at the seashore. In another the god of poetry Aonghus Og made her pregnant. At birth Noine spoke nine mysterious sayings. His grandfather died soon after. The pattern calls to mind the hero Lugh and the evil-eyed Balor, his cruel grandfather. Several scholars believe his tales fed those of Fionn Mac Cumhaill.
